page_hint: Chapter 10, §3 Worked Example, Data Parallelism: Replicating, Then Syncing Gradients
quoted_clause: for N=8 the per-rank send volume is (N-1)/N × 280 ≈ 245 GB and the send-plus-receive total is 1.75 × 280 ≈ 490 GB ... At 25 GB/s (single 200Gb/s link) that is 245 / 25 ≈ 9.8 s per step ... At the H100 NVLink directional peak of 450 GB/s, the same ideal ring estimate is 245/450 ≈ 0.54 s
observed: The 280 GB FP32 gradient case reuses the 140 GB FP16 gradient traffic numbers from Chapter 9. For a ring all-reduce with M=280 GB and N=8, the total per-rank send volume is 2*(N-1)/N*M = 490 GB, not 245 GB; the per-rank receive volume is also 490 GB, and send-plus-receive is 980 GB, not 490 GB.
evidence: Reduce-scatter sends (N-1)/N*M = 245 GB per rank; all-gather sends another (N-1)/N*M = 245 GB per rank. Total send = 490 GB. 490/25 = 19.6 s; 490/450 ≈ 1.09 s. The printed 245/25 and 245/450 are the Chapter 9 140 GB values, not the 280 GB values.
root_cause: The precision basis was changed from 140 GB FP16 to 280 GB FP32, but the downstream ring traffic and time calculations were not doubled.
correction: Either state that 245 GB is the one-phase send volume and give the full two-phase send volume as 490 GB with times 19.6 s at 25 GB/s and ≈1.09 s at 450 GB/s, or explicitly keep the 140 GB FP16 example for the 9.8 s / 0.54 s numbers. Do not mix 280 GB logical size with 140 GB traffic arithmetic.
acceptance_test: Recompute from M=280 GB, N=8: printed per-rank total send, total receive, send-plus-receive, and both bandwidth times must match 490 GB, 490 GB, 980 GB, 19.6 s, and ≈1.09 s respectively, or the text must clearly label 245 GB as one-phase only and use 490 GB for total send time.

quoted_clause: If the architecture calls for data-parallel training of a 70B FP16 model across 8 nodes (an eight-rank DP group, e.g. one rank per node), the all-reduce bandwidth dictates whether the nodes are connected by InfiniBand, 200 GbE, or even 100 GbE. If the budget can accommodate NVLink-equipped hosts (GPUs connected on-node), keeping the all-reduce on-node gives an ideal ring time about 1/11th the assumed InfiniBand case and about 1/180th the assumed RoCE case
observed: For the stated eight-node, one-rank-per-node DP group, the all-reduce is an inter-node collective. The 1/11 and 1/180 ratios compare an eight-rank group placed on one NVLink host with an eight-rank group placed across hosts; they do not apply to the same eight-node one-rank-per-node DP group.
evidence: Chapter 9 §3 computes 0.54 s for an eight-rank NVLink ring and 6.1 s / 98 s for eight-rank cross-host rings. If the DP group has one rank per node across 8 nodes, the ranks are not on one NVLink domain; NVLink can only help intra-node subgroups or a different rank placement.
root_cause: The paragraph conflates two different rank placements: an 8-rank on-node DP group and an 8-node one-rank-per-node DP group.
correction: Reword to separate the cases: for the stated 8-node one-rank-per-node DP group, the all-reduce is inter-node; the 1/11 and 1/180 figures apply only if the 8-rank DP group is placed within one NVLink host, or to the intra-node portion of a hierarchical DP design.
acceptance_test: A reader should not be able to infer that an 8-node one-rank-per-node DP all-reduce can be kept on NVLink; the text must explicitly state which rank placement the ratios describe.

page_hint: Chapter 12, §8 Mini-Case, Candidate (b); also Table 12-1 row (b)
quoted_clause: up to ~576 GB (140 + 436) at the canonical per-host KV budget (§12.3)
observed: This is inconsistent with §12.3, which says the canonical per-host KV budget is 640 - 140 weights - ~64 runtime ≈ 436 GB, and that 140 + 436 + ~64 = 640 GB exactly. 576 GB is weights plus KV only; it excludes the ~64 GB runtime reserve.
evidence: 140 + 436 = 576; 576 + 64 = 640. Table 12-1 also says "~576 GB at the full KV budget (140 + 436)", while §12.3 says the full pool is 640 GB including runtime.
root_cause: The mini-case and table summarize the full KV budget as weights+KV only, while the main text includes runtime in the 640 GB pool total.
correction: Make the quantity explicit: "weights+KV = 576 GB; including the ~64 GB runtime reserve, the host total is 640 GB" or change the total to 640 GB if the sentence is about whole-host residency.
acceptance_test: Every statement of Candidate (b) full-KV residency must agree on whether 576 GB or 640 GB is being quoted, and 640 GB must include the ~64 GB runtime component.

page_hint: Chapter 9, §5 Common Mistakes, "Ignoring contention from other traffic"
quoted_clause: if other collectives (e.g., all-gather for optimizer state) are running simultaneously
observed: FSDP-style training all-gathers parameter shards, not optimizer state. Optimizer state is sharded and updated locally; it is not the object normally all-gathered.
evidence: Chapter 10 states FSDP "all-gathers parameter shards" in forward and "reduce-scatters gradients" in backward. The same chapter's FSDP example uses a 64 MiB unit all-gather, not optimizer-state all-gather.
root_cause: Imprecise example of a concurrent collective.
correction: Replace with "all-gather for parameter shards (FSDP)" or "reduce-scatter for gradients".
acceptance_test: The example collective must correspond to a real FSDP/DP training communication pattern.

quoted_clause: MoE models (if chosen per Ch3) push toward EP, because the full expert set must be resident (the active count sets compute per token, not residency) and EP shards the experts across GPUs.
observed: "Must be resident" is too absolute. The same chapter later says the total expert residency must be sharded only "if the deployment keeps all experts resident in HBM", and that expert offloading or caching changes the capacity calculus.
evidence: Chapter 10 §7: "the total expert residency that must be sharded if the deployment keeps all experts resident in HBM (expert offloading or caching otherwise changes the capacity calculus)".
root_cause: The architecture-consequence bullet omits the residency assumption used later.
correction: Add the condition: "when the deployment keeps the full expert set resident in HBM" or "for HBM-resident expert placements".
acceptance_test: The sentence must not imply that offloaded or cached expert deployments necessarily require all experts to be resident in HBM.

page_hint: Chapter 11, §6 Architecture Consequence, baseline bullet; also §5 Common Mistakes
quoted_clause: PagedAttention packs the ~24.1 GB-per-request KV densely (fixed-size pages, minimal fragmentation) so more concurrent requests fit in the 640 GB node
observed: PagedAttention reduces external fragmentation and over-reservation, but block-level internal fragmentation and metadata overhead remain. "Minimal fragmentation" and the related "removes the fragmentation tax" can be read as eliminating all fragmentation.
evidence: Chapter 11 §2 says PagedAttention "reduces external fragmentation and over-reservation, improving effective KV capacity; block-level internal fragmentation and metadata overhead remain."
root_cause: Shorthand conflates all fragmentation with external fragmentation.
correction: Use "reduces external fragmentation; block-level internal fragmentation and metadata overhead remain" in both locations.
acceptance_test: No sentence should state or imply that PagedAttention removes all KV fragmentation.

quoted_clause: Latency/geography: SLO can't be met due to distance or contention → split prefill/decode (a within-tier move).
observed: P/D disaggregation addresses phase contention and mismatched resource binding, not network distance or geography. Distance is a placement problem (edge/region/local), not a P/D problem.
evidence: The same paragraph says "moving the serving edge closer (local) is a placement move to a lower rung, not a climb trigger".
root_cause: Two different causes (distance and contention) are merged into one trigger with one remedy.
correction: Split the trigger: "contention/phase interference → P/D disaggregation" and "distance/geography → placement to a lower or different tier, or regional replicas".
acceptance_test: A reader should map distance to placement, not to P/D disaggregation.

quoted_clause: because the architect climbed the ladder precisely one rung
observed: The canonical 40 rps workload was already described as a fleet of ~21 server-class hosts, i.e. a cluster of server-class hosts. At 100 rps the deployment remains a cluster, just larger. "Climbed precisely one rung" can imply moving from a single server to a cluster, which may not match the prior canonical deployment.
evidence: Chapter 13 §3: "the canonical enterprise-Q&A RAG workload sits on the server tier as a fleet of ~21 server-class hosts at the 40 rps peak ... the traffic scaling is a cluster of server-class hosts".
root_cause: The mini-case does not state whether the prior on-prem service was a single server or the 21-host cluster.
correction: Clarify the prior deployment size. If it was already a 21-host cluster, say the architect "scaled within the cluster tier"; if it was a single server, say so explicitly before using "one rung".
acceptance_test: The rung language must match the stated prior and new tiers.

quoted_clause: Total fleet cost $155.8K/mo (21 hosts) ÷ $15K = ~10.4× over the total budget
observed: "10.4× over" is ambiguous or incorrect. The cost is 10.4 times the budget; the excess over the budget is 9.4 times the budget.
evidence: 155.8 / 15 = 10.39. Later in the same paragraph the text correctly says "~10.4× the stakeholder's stated $15,000 total monthly budget".
root_cause: Wording conflates "times the budget" with "times over the budget".
correction: Use "10.4× the total budget" or "9.4× over the total budget".
acceptance_test: The ratio wording must match the arithmetic: cost/budget = 10.4, not excess/budget = 10.4.

page_hint: Chapter 13, §3 Worked Example, Escalating: When 10×Traffic Forces the Cluster Tier
quoted_clause: the ~2.0 rps screen uses the unfloored 17.5-slot quotient and applies no utilization headroom, so 50 hosts could only deliver 50 × 17/8.6 ≈ 98.8 rps — below demand.
observed: The sentence says the screen uses the unfloored 17.5-slot quotient, but the calculation uses the floored 17 slots. With 17.5 slots, 50 hosts deliver 50 × 17.5 / 8.6 ≈ 101.7 rps, not 98.8 rps.
root_cause: The explanation mixes the unfloored and floored slot counts in the same sentence.
correction: State both clearly: using the conservative floored 17 slots, 50 hosts deliver 98.8 rps; using 17.5 slots, they deliver ~101.7 rps but with no utilization headroom and based on a rounded 2.0 rps figure.
acceptance_test: The slot count used in the arithmetic must match the slot count named in the sentence.

quoted_clause: ✗ ~4 avg / ~15 peak hosts at the single-H100 rate (Table 12-2)
observed: Candidate (c) is laid out as 1×H100 and Table 12-2 sizes it in "H100 cards", not 8-GPU hosts. Calling these "hosts" can be confused with the 8×H100 host unit used for Candidates (a) and (b).
evidence: Table 12-2 says "~4 H100 cards" and "~15 H100 cards", and its units note says "(c) is sized in single H100 cards (one card per 7B instance)".
root_cause: Terminology drift between host and card for single-GPU instances.
correction: Change to "~4 avg / ~15 peak single-H100 cards" or "instances".
acceptance_test: All Candidate (c) capacity units should be cards/instances, not 8-GPU hosts.

quoted_clause: In round r, rank i sends chunk (i−r) mod N in both phases, so rank r ends the reduce-scatter holding reduced chunk r.
observed: The stated send convention does not by itself imply the stated final ownership. A ring reduce-scatter's final chunk ownership depends on the receive direction and which local chunk is reduced; the caption omits that convention.
evidence: For N=4, if rank i sends chunk i-r to i+1 and receives/reduces chunk i-r-1, the final ownership is offset from the simple "rank r holds chunk r" statement unless the round count and receive rule are specified. The caption's conclusion may be off by one under the usual convention.
root_cause: The caption states a send formula and a final-ownership conclusion without the intermediate receive/reduce rule needed to make the conclusion follow.
correction: Add the explicit convention, e.g. "rank i receives chunk i-r-1 from i-1 and reduces it with its local copy; after N-1 rounds rank i holds reduced chunk i+1" (or adjust the formula so the stated conclusion is true).
acceptance_test: A 4-rank simulation using the caption's exact send/receive/reduce convention must produce the stated final chunk ownership.

quoted_clause: When a GPU is idle waiting, we reach for DP (more work per GPU); CP addresses long-sequence/KV capacity, not idle-fill.
observed: DP does not make an idle single GPU do more work; it adds independent replicas or increases total batch across devices. If a GPU is idle because arrivals are low, DP does not fill that GPU. If it is idle because the batch is small, the direct levers are batch size, microbatching, or continuous batching, not necessarily DP.
evidence: Chapter 10 defines inference DP as "independent replicas each serve a disjoint set of requests" and training DP as "replicates all weights on every GPU, feeds each a different batch".
root_cause: The resource-triangle heuristic conflates aggregate throughput scaling with per-GPU idle-fill.
correction: Reword to: "When aggregate throughput is limited by batch size and the model fits, DP adds replicas/total batch; it is not a per-GPU idle-fill mechanism."
acceptance_test: A reader should not infer that DP fills an underloaded single GPU.

quoted_clause: The head-divisibility requirement for the Ulysses strategy is stated in Wan's official README at commit 9737cba9c1c3c4d04b33fcad41c111989865d315
observed: The main text applies the divisibility requirement to Wan2.2's official multi-GPU path, but the cited source for the divisibility statement is a Wan2.1 README. The Wan2.2 citation supports the FSDP+Ulysses path, not necessarily the exact divisibility requirement for Wan2.2.
evidence: The footnote cites Wan2.2 README for "Multi-GPU inference using FSDP + DeepSpeed Ulysses" and Wan2.1 README for "num_heads should be divisible by ulysses_size".
root_cause: Source support mismatch between the version in the claim and the version of the cited requirement.
correction: Cite a Wan2.2 source for the divisibility requirement, or qualify: "documented for Wan2.1/Ulysses; re-verify for the deployed Wan2.2 configuration."
acceptance_test: The cited source for the divisibility requirement must match the model version in the claim, or the claim must be version-qualified.

quoted_clause: de-escalate when 30-day p95 utilization < 40% AND SLO margin > 2× AND the smaller tier's failure domain is acceptable.
observed: "SLO margin > 2×" is not computable without a denominator. It could mean 2× headroom in latency, 2× utilization margin, or something else.
evidence: The caption gives no definition of the quantity being multiplied by 2.
root_cause: Shorthand threshold left undefined.
correction: Define the metric, e.g. "p95 latency ≤ 0.5× SLO" or "SLO headroom > 2× current p95 latency".
acceptance_test: The threshold must be expressible as a measurable inequality.

page_hint: Chapter 11, §6 Architecture Consequence, "Beyond a node" bullet
quoted_clause: when prefill FLOPs and decode bandwidth fight on one pool, P/D disaggregation (Splitwise/DistServe/Mooncake) is the architecture of choice
observed: "Architecture of choice" is too strong. P/D disaggregation is a candidate that pays off only when measured phase interference and KV-transfer cost justify it; other options (more hosts, chunked prefill, scheduling changes, prefix caching) may be better.
evidence: Earlier in the same chapter: "it pays off when measured prefill/decode interference binds — evaluate it against measured phase conflict, not topology alone".
root_cause: The conclusion is stated as a default rather than a conditional, measurement-dependent choice.
correction: Reword to "a candidate architecture when measured phase interference and KV-transfer cost justify it".
acceptance_test: No sentence should present P/D disaggregation as the automatic choice without the measurement condition.

quoted_clause: This is the number that, multiplied by the number of devices in the candidate layout, must exceed the workload's tokens-per-second demand
observed: Linear multiplication by device count is valid for independent data-parallel replicas, but not for TP/PP/EP layouts where communication, partitioning, and synchronization change the per-device contribution to host throughput.
evidence: Chapter 10 explains TP/PP/EP communication costs; Chapter 12 itself uses per-host prefill rates for 8×H100 layouts rather than a simple per-GPU sum for model-parallel candidates.
root_cause: Missing parallelism-mode qualifier in the throughput gate.
correction: Specify: "for data-parallel replicas, multiply by replica count; for TP/PP/EP, use the measured per-host or per-layout goodput, not a simple per-device sum."
acceptance_test: The statement must distinguish DP replication from model-parallel layouts.

page_hint: Ch16 §3 Worked Example, Mode 2 cloud GPU instances, H_required equation
quoted_clause: H_required = ∫_0^T N_required(t) dt + N_warm·T_warm + R_reserved; H_paid ≥ H_required ... N_required(t) is the number of hosts that must be running at time t
observed: The equation adds warm-pool and reserved host-hours to the integral of N_required(t), but N_required(t) is defined as the number of hosts that must be running at time t. If N_required(t) already includes warm and reserved hosts, the separate terms double-count them. If N_required(t) is meant to exclude them, the definition is wrong. The following sentence 'H_required already includes the warm-pool and reservation terms' contradicts the displayed addition.
evidence: Let N_required(t) be total required running hosts. Then ∫ N_required(t) dt already includes N_warm·T_warm and R_reserved for the times those hosts are running. Adding them again counts the same host-hours twice. Conversely, if the integral is meant to be burst-only, the definition 'number of hosts that must be running at time t' is too broad.
root_cause: Ambiguous variable definition in the cloud occupancy model: total required hosts versus incremental burst hosts above warm/reserved capacity.
correction: Either (a) define N_required(t) as total required running hosts and remove the separate N_warm·T_warm and R_reserved terms, or (b) define N_burst(t) as additional hosts above the warm/reserved baseline and write H_required = ∫ N_burst(t) dt + N_warm·T_warm + R_reserved. Make the prose match the equation.
acceptance_test: The cloud host-hour equation counts each warm, reserved, and burst host-hour exactly once, and the definition of the integrated variable matches the terms added to it.

page_hint: Ch15 §1 Concept, canonical SLO sentence; compare Ch14 §3 and Ch14 §8
quoted_clause: TPOT ≤ 40 ms (Ch 4/Ch 14)
observed: Ch15 states the canonical SLO as 'TPOT ≤ 40 ms' and cites Ch4/Ch14. In this chunk, Ch14 repeatedly uses a 25 ms TPOT target: 'TPOT ~25 ms/token', 'TPOT p50/p95 (≤ ~25 ms median)', and 'median TPOT about 25 ms'. There is no visible 40 ms TPOT SLO in Ch14, and the percentile qualification is missing in Ch15.
evidence: Ch14 §3: '~9,200 input tokens ... + ~300 output, TTFT budget (median ≤ 1.2 s, p95 ≤ 2 s), TPOT ~25 ms/token.' Ch14 §8: 'The SLO remains median TTFT ≤ 1.2 s, p95 TTFT ≤ 2 s and median TPOT about 25 ms.' Ch15 §1: 'TTFT median ≤ 1.2 s, p95 ≤ 2 s, TPOT ≤ 40 ms (Ch 4/Ch 14).'
root_cause: Cross-chapter drift in the canonical TPOT SLO and missing percentile qualification (median vs p95).
correction: Align the canonical TPOT SLO. If the intended SLO is median TPOT ≤ 25 ms and p95 TPOT ≤ 40 ms, state both explicitly in Ch14 and Ch15. If only one value is canonical, use that value in both chapters and remove the incorrect cross-reference.
acceptance_test: Ch14 and Ch15 use the same percentile-qualified TPOT SLO, and any citation to Ch14 for a 40 ms TPOT bound is either supported by Ch14 text or removed.

page_hint: Ch15 'Two Mechanisms, Read as Mechanisms', speculative decoding paragraph
quoted_clause: the expensive part of decode is not the arithmetic per token but the serialization — each target-model step streams the weights from HBM
observed: This presents decode as dominated by weight streaming/serialization rather than arithmetic without qualifying batch size or operating point. At low batch sizes this is often true, but at larger batches decode can become compute-bound or mixed. The book's own standard is to avoid making 'decode is bandwidth-bound' a universal law.
evidence: The sentence uses 'the expensive part of decode' as a general mechanism explanation. Earlier in Ch15, the text correctly says whether a phase is compute- or bandwidth-bound is a property of model × workload × kernel × hardware operating point. The speculative-decoding paragraph does not carry that qualification.
root_cause: A first-order low-batch decode model is stated as a general decode property.
correction: Qualify the statement, e.g.: 'At low batch sizes, the dominant decode cost is often weight streaming rather than arithmetic; at higher batches, arithmetic can dominate. In the low-batch regime, if the draft can propose k tokens...' or add a cross-reference to the roofline/operating-point discussion.
acceptance_test: The speculative-decoding explanation does not assert that decode's expensive part is universally serialization; it states the condition under which weight streaming dominates.
